scenario: Here's the design doc for our Shared Documents feature (design.md). Threat model it before we start building.
fixture: evaluations/fixtures/threat-modeler/design.md (multi-tenant SaaS design doc with six planted security weaknesses)
required_behaviors: draws a data-flow diagram (text or Mermaid) covering the browser, app, Postgres, S3, thumbnail queue/worker and the external import URL, with trust boundaries explicitly marked
identifies Import from URL as server-side request forgery, naming cloud metadata credential theft (169.254.169.254 / task role) or internal-service access as the impact
identifies /share/<doc_id> with sequential IDs and no token as enumerable by anonymous users across tenants (IDOR), and proposes an unguessable revocable share token

identifies serving uploads from app.teamboard.io with the user-supplied Content-Type as stored XSS against users and the same-origin admin console, and proposes a separate content domain and/or forced attachment with server-set type
produces prioritized mitigations mapped to threat IDs and turned into testable security requirements with test cases
forbidden_behaviors: a generic STRIDE checklist whose threats do not reference specific components of this design (import, share links, /view, ImageMagick worker, presigned uploads)
rating every threat the same severity
grading_notes: Compare against evaluations/answers/threat-modeler.md, which lists all six planted weaknesses (SSRF, enumerable share links, same-origin user content, unsandboxed ImageMagick, unbounded presigned uploads, missing audit log) with expected mitigations. Pass requires all five required_behaviors. Note in grading how many of weaknesses 4-6 were also found; a strong run finds all six.
